title.narrative: Accountable Governance for Basic Service Delivery

description.narrative: The PDO is to improve resource management, transparency and accountability of government systems for enabling the delivery of local development projects and basic services.

The development objective of the Accountable Governance for Basic Service Delivery Project for Sierra Leone is to improve resource management, transparency, and accountability of government systems for enabling the delivery of local development projects and basic services. The project comprises of four components. The first component, systems and skills for local service delivery will focus on improving key systems at central and local levels to support service delivery. It consists of following sub-components: (i) better public financial management (PFM) systems at the central and local level; (ii) improved procurement systems; (iii) improved capacity of key technical staff at local council (LCs); and (iv) effective local audits and external oversight. The second component, local development financing aim to directly support LC financing. It consists of following sub-components: (i) local government development grants; (ii) improved systems for LC financing; and (iii) contingent emergency response component (CERC). The third component, integrated data platforms for monitoring and accountability will support the government's proposed reforms to improve data management and reporting at the local level through targeted support to LCs, as well as data on critical service-delivery inputs in the priority sectors It consists of following sub-components: (i) improved systems for LC monitoring and reporting; (ii) robust supply-chain data platforms for key commodities; and (iii) supporting the demonstration effect of using data platforms for results reporting and decision-making at local level to support development and operationalization of national monitoring and evaluation (M and E) management information system (NaMEMIS). The fourth component, project management and implementation support will cover the costs of managing the project as well as the specific activities for project M and E, communication, and outreach.

condition.narrative: The Recipient shall not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, establish and thereafter maintain throughout Projectimplementation, a Project Steering Committee (PSC), responsible for overseeing the Project, approving Annual Work Plans and Budget,reviewing Project progress reports, and ensuring that Project objectives are being met. (Schedule 2, Section I, A , 3, (a) )

The Recipient shall not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, recruit on a competitive basis and thereaftermaintain throughout implementation of the Project, a financial management specialist, a procurement specialist and a financialmanagement officer, with experience, qualifications, and terms of reference satisfactory to the Association (Schedule 2, Section I,A , 1, (c) )

The Recipient shall prepare and furnish to the Association not later than November 30 of each Fiscal Year during the implementationof the Project, a work plan and budget containing all the activities proposed to be included in the Project during the followingFiscal Year, and a proposed financing plan for expenditures required for such activities, setting forth the proposed amounts andsources of financing; except for the annual work plan and budget for the Project for the first year of Project implementation,which shall be furnished no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date (Schedule 2, Section I, B, 3, (a) )

The Recipient shall, no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date: (a) recruit and thereafter maintain throughout theimplementation of the Project an internal auditor, who will be part of the PMU staff, with qualifications, experience and terms ofreference satisfactory to the association; and (b) develop an internal audit plan satisfactory to the Association (Schedule 2,Section IV, 2)

The Recipient shall, no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date, install an accounting software within the PFMU in formand substance satisfactory to the Association (Schedule 2, Section IV, 1)

title.narrative: Component 1 IRI 9: Establish joint CSO-local government Feedback and Accountability frameworks for monitoring and sharing of information on development projects and service delivery.
Procurement transactions executed through e-GP in seven ministries, departments and agencies of government

comment.narrative:
The first measurable target is in 2026 - i.e, 10 per cent procurement transactions conducted through the eGP system by MDAs to which the system is rolled out. Development of the eGP system is ongoing and the expected go-live dat is in 2026. The end target is 40 per cent.
The calculation of the actual will be based on transactions executed using the eGP system against the total number of procurement transactions uploaded in the system. The targets have been revised to reflect delays encountered and alignment with the DPO indicator target.

title.narrative: District Councils that have mainstreamed community participation (40 percent female participation) during planning, budgeting process and in end-of-year reporting of budget execution

comment.narrative:
This revised indicator now measures two components: (i) mainstreaming community participation in local development planning through expansion of the BASE Initiative; and (ii) mainstreaming community participation during the annula budget process and end-of-year reporting of budget execution.
Both component of the indicator measures measure female participation - with a target of 40 per cent.
Indicator Targets for 2025 Implementation Year are 8 and 12 for component 1 and 2 respectively. Achievement as of April 2025 are (0)(15) for the budget process and end-of-year reporting for the 2024 FY.
Component one of this indicator relates to the BASE Consortium and USAID, scaling from 6 to 8 local councils, excluding WARDC. WARDC plan will be reviewed in 2026 taking the total to 9 DDPs that will be supported through the BASE support.
